To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
highly active antiretoviral therapy improves end‐stage liver‐disease‐free survival in patients co‐infected with human immunodeficiency and hepatitis C virus.
highly active antiretoviral therapy (HAAR) improves end stage liver disease‐free survival in human immunodeficienct virus/hepatitis C virus co‐infection.
HIV+ men on HAART have significantly better ESLD‐free survivals, compared to HAART‐untreated HIV+ and HIV− men.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of highly active anti‐retroviral therapy on progression to end stage liver disease in HIV/hepatitis C co‐infection.
the impact of HAART on progression to end-stage liver disease (ESDL) in HIV/hepatitis C virus co-infection.
the impact of highly active anti-retroviral therapy (HA-ART) on progression of hepatitis C virus (HVC) infection in patients with HIV-HCV co-infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HAART improves survival in HIV‐infected patients with HCV‐related cirrhosis.
HAART improves survival in HIV+ HCV+ patients with haemophilia, but does not prevent the development of ESLD.
highly active antiretoviral therapy (HAAR) does not appear to have any significant effect on the development of end‐stage liver failure in co‐infected patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
highly active antiretoviral therapy improves ESLDFree survival in HIVHCV co infection, approaching that in HCV monoinfection.
HAART reduces ESLD progression and death from AIDS in HCV/HIV co‐infected men, with a similar effect on overall mortality as in HIV− men.
HAART improves liver disease‐free survival in HCV+ haemo‐HIV men.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV‐positive patients with HCV infection who are treated with antiretrovial therapy (ART) have a survival rate that is comparable to HIV‐negative patients.
HIV+ HAART treated patients have a survival similar to that of HIV− patients.
HIV+ men on HAART have a survival similar to that of HIV− men.
